settings.headline: How long does numbing cream last?
settings.subhead: Duration depends on the procedure, the tier, and the individual. The honest answer isn't a number — it's a framework that matches the appointment. Senseless tiers are formulated to match the session lengths they're built for.
settings.image_alt: Editorial close-up of a Senseless topical preparation on a warm off-white background

settings.headline: Three things shape the window.
settings.body: The procedure: a 15-minute Botox session asks something different from a 90-minute microneedling appointment. The tier: Clinical, Advanced, and Professional are formulated for different session lengths. The individual: skin sensitivity, treatment area, hydration, and the specific application all change what the same product does on the same procedure for two different clients. The duration question can't be answered with a single number because none of these variables are constant.
settings.image_alt: Editorial still life of the Senseless range — the three duration-shaping variables

settings.body: Topical preparations for aesthetic procedures are designed to cover a typical appointment window — your practitioner can advise on timing for your treatment. Within the Senseless system, the tiers are formulated to match the session lengths they're built for — Clinical for shorter, focused appointments; Advanced for longer or more sensitive sessions; Professional for sustained or intensive bookings. The system's logic is built into the duration question, even if the specific timing isn't ours to give.

settings.headline: How long does it take to work?
settings.body:
Onset is a separate question from duration, and it has the same honest answer: it depends on the procedure, the tier, and your practitioner's protocol. Anyone quoting a single number for every appointment is over-simplifying. The application window is set by the person doing your treatment — ask them how far in advance to prepare, and let their guidance take precedence.

Within the Senseless system the tier is matched to the session, and your practitioner's timing is matched to your booking. That's the framework, and the routing back to the person who knows your procedure.

settings.headline: What clients book.
settings.body:
These are typical session lengths, not duration-of-effect claims. The preparation needs to match the session.

Lip Fillers. 15–30 minutes typically. Clinical Strength fits this comfortably.

Botox. 10–20 minutes. The shortest aesthetic procedure. Clinical or even no preparation suits most clients.

Microneedling. 30–90 minutes for a full-face session. Advanced is the recommended tier for this length.

Laser (face zones). 15–45 minutes typically. Advanced suits most face laser sessions.

Laser (body, resurfacing). 30 minutes to 2+ hours. Advanced spray or Professional for the longest sessions.

SPMU. 60–120+ minutes — sustained sittings. Advanced or Professional, with reapplication sometimes used during the session.

settings.headline: Most appointments are timed to fit.
settings.body: A well-matched preparation is chosen for the length of the procedure. The reason the Senseless system has three tiers and the recommendation matrix tells you which to pick is exactly this — too short a window for an intensive session is the most common application mistake. If your appointment runs longer than expected and you've been on the lighter side of preparation, your practitioner has options. Some reapply at the chair. Some use additional numbing during the procedure. Some pause briefly. Your practitioner knows what they can offer and what their protocol allows.
settings.image_alt: Editorial detail of a Senseless preparation tube matched to session length

settings.heading: When to ask your practitioner
settings.body: Specific duration windows are part of every aesthetic practitioner's protocol. They know how long their procedures run, what preparation they use, and what to do if a client's preparation runs short. Ask in advance. The clinic that runs your appointment is the source of truth for duration questions tied to your specific booking.

settings.question: Will it last through my whole appointment?
settings.answer: If you've matched the tier to the procedure, that's what the system is designed for. If you've chosen a lighter tier than the procedure asks for, the window may not cover the full session. Pick the tier the procedure calls for.

settings.question: Does the higher tier last longer or work harder?
settings.answer: The higher tiers are formulated for procedures that ask more of the preparation. Different strengths, different formulation context. They're not "stronger versions" of Clinical — they're matched to longer or more demanding sessions.

settings.question: What if my appointment runs over?
settings.answer: Most practitioners have protocols for this. Some reapply, some use additional preparation at the chair. Ask in advance what your practitioner's approach is.

settings.question: How does Senseless compare to other brands?
settings.answer: We don't make comparative duration claims. Senseless is a UK cosmetic topical preparation, CPSR assessed.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product. Not a medicine. Not a pharmacy product.
